newsitem.title: EGYPT: Sudan rebel leader warns Arakis Corp on oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebel leader warns Arakis Corp on oil deal.

text.p: Sudanese rebel leader Colonel John Garang warned Canada's Arakis Energy Corp that his forces would strike if needed to halt any attempts to develop its concessions in southern Sudan that would benefit the Khartoum government.

Arakis announced earlier this month it was close to signing a deal with other firms to develop its Heglig and Unity fields in Sudan and build a 900-mile pipeline to the Red Sea from the fields. The Sudanese government will refine the oil.

"If they succeed in extracting oil then this will...give the government more money and so it would have more funding for war. But we will not allow this to happen and we will strike at these operations," Garang, head of the Sudan People Liberation Army (SPLA), told the Arabic-language daily Al-Hayat.

"We have warned Arakis of the consequences of trying to work in southern Sudan. We clearly told them we will shut down their operation... we can assure them that we will stop whatever stage they are in," Garang said in an interview published on Friday.
The SPLA is the largest and oldest southern Sudanese rebel group fighting for greater independence for the mainly Christian and animist south of Sudan from the Moslem, Arabised north.

In July, the SPLA-United said Arakis was colluding with Khartoum and warned them to leave southern Sudan. It added that it would not allow the Khartoum government to "steal" oil from the Adar-1 field and move it by barges on the White Nile river.

Garang said rebel forces were now controlling the Eastern Equatoria province and up north towards Feshlah, adding that a newly-formed committee by the Eritrean-based opposition groups to coordinate military operations against the Islamist government was ready to strike at Khartoum.

"Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir has challenged us, saying 'I am ready for you, come' and we say that we are more ready than he is. And we're going to strike hard and Bashir just won't know what hit him," Garang said.
"We are currently planning the steps we will take to advance towards Khartoum," he added.
The rebel war has killed hundreds of thousands of people and has also displaced and sent into exile many more. It has also drained the government's already limited resources.

In Khartoum, Sudan's government spokesman dubbed the opposition war council a "desperate measure which reflects the confusion of the treacherous opposition in the face of the success of the government in building peace from within."
